utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have appearances for the afternoon starting with the Prosecution, please. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel. Mark Harmon, Lorna Bolton, April Carter, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, and for the Defence, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours and everyone in the courtroom. Mr. Perisic is represented today by Milos Andric, Tina Drolec, Chad Mair, our case manager Daniela Tasic, and Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith and Novak Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Good afternoon, Mr. Jusufovic. Just to remind that you are still bound by the declaration that you made at the beginning of your testimony yesterday to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: There are just two areas of your previous testimony that I would like to go back to from cross-examination. The first area, sir, concerned questioning - and for the record, this is found at page 3247 of the transcript - where you were being asked about receiving calls from former members of the fire brigade, and you told the Court that you had conversations with former members, and they would say things like, A shell is coming your way; or they would be announcing that five more shells were coming -- or going to fall on the station. Do you remember that portion of the questioning from yesterday, sir?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I just want to ask you some questions about that. First of all, from whom -- what former members of the fire brigade did you receive calls?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was Zeljko Rakanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And did you receive calls every time there was going to be shelling or just on occasion?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They did not call every time, just on occasion, because they used the same radio sets that we had, so from time to time they would announce the shelling. They would curse us and say, Now we're going to start shelling you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. So my next question was going to be, were these in the nature of friendly warnings or different kinds of calls?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they cursed us. They used profanities. They would tell us that they would kill us all and that's why they were sending these shells. It wasn't in a friendly manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And the other area, sir, had to do with questioning about the cold storage depot and the slaughter house. Do you recall that area of questioning from yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could bring up Defence Exhibit 41 from yesterday, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, you recall being asked questions about this document yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked about Magros here, not about the slaughter house.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: All right. So this is a different -- this is a different facility than the -- sorry, the Hladnjaca cold storage?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a different document when they asked me about the cold storage facility.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I have the wrong exhibit number, then, I think. Must have been Exhibit 42, D42. If that could be produced, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Great. I have the right document now, do I. Sir?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the right document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And as I understand it, you indicated yesterday that this was -- you acknowledge this was an order about military use of the premises at Hladnjaca cold storage, and the date appears to be sometime in September, perhaps September 18th, 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says on the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And we were -- when you were answering questions yesterday about the fire at the Hladnjaca cold storage, you had indicated that you had been injured at the time of that fire and could not personally attend. Could you tell us what month and year your fire brigade responded to the fire at Hladnjaca?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in August 1992, and this document is dated September 1993, so when we put out the fire in 1992, it is certain that there was no military presence in that facility.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Those are all of my questions. The Court may have some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just one or two questions for you, sir. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where in Bosnia-Herzegovina is Vratnik?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vratnik is in the -- in Sarajevo town. It's the old part of Sarajevo, a little bit above Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much. Now, yesterday, and unlike Madam Bolton I'm technologically challenged, so I'm not going to be able to give you the correct page number of transcript. I give it to you as it stood yesterday. At page 79, lines 18 to 20, you indicated that you had been a fire-fighter since 1983. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And in the answer to the next question, you said had you been a taxi driver from 1980 to 1986. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. That's correct. I don't know what you said, what year I became a fire-fighter. I became a fire-fighter in 1986.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good. That's what I wanted to correct -- I wanted to check, because according to the transcript you said -- it said 1983. I don't know what you may have said. So it was 1986 when you became a fire-fighter?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a professional fire-fighter. I became a professional fire-fighter in 1986. But I was a volunteer fire-fighter since the age of 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And -- okay. Now, if you were a volunteer fire-fighter since the age of 7, then my question will still stand. In 1983, were you still a volunteer fire-fighter?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was a volunteer fire-fighter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And at that time, your permanent job was as a taxi driver?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: As a volunteer fire-fighter, under what circumstances do you go and fight the fires, if you are supposed to be driving a taxi? Can you explain how that happened? How did you hold these two jobs.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was, by occupation, a taxi driver, and a volunteer fire-fighter meant that when there was a fire to be put out, they would call us volunteers, volunteer fire-fighters, and we would set our jobs aside and come to the fire station, and then we would go to respond to the fire. So it was all on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. That clears that up. Now, this may be a little difficult, and I will ask for assistance from those who can put me to that page. It was page 82, lines 24, to page 83, line 2. You said something like: When we were there we didn't have anything. That's just about all I wrote of that sentence, so I'm not able to give you the meat of that sentence. What I wanted to find out from you is, where were you, and what were you doing there? How do I get yesterday's page 82?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well -- I thought I had it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The registrar will help me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If it will assist, it was -- I think that was the question I objected to or around that point in time. So if we searched for the objection, that might assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, that's page 3248 at line 11. It says: "While I was there, we didn't have anything. We would observe from Lapusnica them shelling us. This was from about 800 metres, and we would just lie there because there was nothing you could shell" -- "we could shell them with or there was nothing we could shoot and reach them." Do you remember that answer? I seem to suspect this was when you were in your trenches with your -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now when you say when you were there, do you mean when you were in the trenches, or what did you mean by "when we were there"?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were on a location which was medieval fort, actually, which is where Vratnik starts, and from this fort you could see Lapusnica. Now, Serbian soldiers were on top of Lapusnica. They played football, they would sunbathe, and then from time to time they would fire a shell from their mortar. We did not have any weapons, and although they were only 800 metres away, we had nothing to shoot at them with or fire at them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Madam Bolton, do you have any questions arising from the Bench's questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I don't. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, that brings us to the end of your testimony. Thank you so much for taking the time to come and testify. You are now excused. You may stand down, and please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is my only witness for today. If I could be excused, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You might just be allowed to leave with some of us when we do just now in case we are ordered to do so. I guess the next witness is a protected witness, and I'm told that there's a little bit of preparation that has to be done before we can call the witness. Is the preparation going to be done while we're here, or are we going to adjourn for two or three minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It takes a minute. You are excused. I suppose that, Madam Carter, you are leading this next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution calls Sead Besic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. While we're waiting for him, can I just explain the protective measures that are granted to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. On 12 February 2007, in the Dragomir Milosevic case, this witness was granted the protection of image distortion, and we're just asking for a continuation of that protective measure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Should we actually be in private session? I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: His identity by name is not at issue. It's merely he wants to have his face protected because he still serves as an officer, so the name and the pseudonym is not necessary, strictly the image itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But was a pseudonym not granted as a protective measures in the previous case?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. In fact, the witness has testified both in the Galic as well as the Dragomir Milosevic case under his given name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. But may we move into private session for the purposes of the witness's entry?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: May I continue with my questioning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Now you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So north is down?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Correct. Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, can you please indicate -- you've written the letter "N," and you've also given a directional angle. Can you please clarify for the Court, are you indicating that to the bottom of this page is north?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Further, with relation to this image, you were asked to mark the impact crater. Can you please do so again here today with a circle.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And if you can please place the English initials "IC" next to the crater.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You further were asked to indicate where the bicycles that we saw in the previous photograph were located within your sketch. Can you please draw a circle around where those bicycles were located?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. If you could please place the English initial "B" above those bicycles.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: If I can have a screen shot of this image and tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The sketch is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P528.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you are done, I have a few clarification questions about the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay. Certainly, Your Honour. That's all I'll need for this sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, within the sketch, you've placed the bicycles and you've placed the impact crater. What is the approximate distance between those two items?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly four metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: That's the only question that I have in relation to this diagram. If Your Honours would like to ask additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Sir, if you could please briefly run us through this sketch and tell us what everything is, it would be very helpful; or maybe let me start off by leading you and say there are two long parallel lines in between of which you have circled the impact crater. What do those lines signify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These parallel lines stand for the width of the street.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name of the street that the witness mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is the name of the street? Did you mention the name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Now, to the top left of the sketch, there is a rectangular drawing with an indentation to the left. What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the edge of the building by which a passage stretches on. This is the entrance way, the lateral entrances into the buildings. If I could only show you this. This street leads to the front gate onto the Markale market.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which street? The street that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It used to be called Vase Miskina Street. Now it's called Ferhadija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the rectangle inside which you wrote the letter "B," what does it represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the town market.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the entrance from the Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street, and then there is the entrance to the market from Ferhadija Street, but you can't see it on this sketch, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to shorten my questions. Do I then understand that the next rectangle on the right is also a block of buildings, and that between it and the one you have just explained, there is a passage again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is another passage also leading to Ferhadija Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. And would I then understand that on the northern side of the street, those are also -- those rectangles also represent buildings and a passage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. There is something that looks like a bicycle or a motorbike. I think it's numbered number 6. What is that? In the street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A driver of a small moped was killed, and the motorcycle was found there and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. You may proceed, Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I would like to call up P526 at page 34, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: For clarity of your answers to Your Honour's questions, are you able to orient on this picture where the motorbike was located in the drawing?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is to be found on the tram tracks here. If I could show it to you, it's on the right-hand side, the spot where the shell landed. There is damage to the left and the right side.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: If I could ask for the assistance of the usher again. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, I'd first like you to circle the motorbike that you referenced in answer to Your Honour's question.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If can you write the English initial "M" to the left of that motor bike.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You were also asked about the impact crater in relation to the sketch. Are you able to see the impact crater in this image as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: The witness is marking the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, if you can write the English initials the "IC" below that impact crater.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You were also asked in relation to Your Honour's question about the buildings themselves. Can you please identify for the Court with the English initials "MM" the Markale market.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, can you also identify for the Court and for counsel what, if any, shrapnel damage is apparent from this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One can see shrapnel damage on the buildings on the left and on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If you could please mark that shrapnel damage with the dashes as you did in the first photograph.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You've marked dashes within the image. If you can please write above those dashes the letter "S," for shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: If I could please have a screen shot of this image and tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought the witness said: "Yes. One can see shrapnel damage on the buildings on the left and on the right side." I would like to see on the other side too.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Before we capture this image, if you can also indicate the shrapnel damage to the right.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we could zoom in, we would be able to see the damage in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in? We can't. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Well, if we can capture this image first and then zoom in, we'll take a second screen shot, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P529.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: If the image can now be zoomed in upon so that we have just the photograph to the extent that we can in the full frame.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, you're now seeing the image. Would you be able to show for Your Honours the shrapnel damage to both the left and right of this image. Before you mark, if you could confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, you've placed both circles as well as dashes to the left and to the right of this image. Are you indicating that this is the shrapnel damage visible at this location?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: To the extent that you're aware, was the shrapnel damage caused on 18 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I would ask to take a screen shot of this image, indicating the shrapnel damage, and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so admitted. May it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P530.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: That is the last image that I'll have marked upon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I just want to clarify one more aspect of your Dragomir Milosevic testimony. As the page numbers have changed from that transcript to this transcript, I want to make certain that we have clarity. During your redirect testimony in Dragomir Milosevic, you were asked about there being evidence of the vendors and their goods being on-site during events at Markale II, and this was at transcript page 2624, line 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I'd now like to call up P526 at page 46.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, is this the image that you identified in Dragomir Milosevic as evidence of a cigarette vendor on-site?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And, finally, I would like to move to page 66 of the same exhibit. Is this the image that you identified in prior testimony as depicting another vendor's goods, specifically cigarette lighters?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, I thank you for your time and your testimony, and I pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have some questions to ask. Just where the covered market, where the bomb exploded on the other side, there is an open market with green grocers who are selling fruits and vegetables.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is some 100 metres away from the market.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The two markets - namely, the open market and the closed-in market - are quite close, one to another, as is the fruit market, which is also nearby.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, the bomb exploded or the shell exploded between the two markets, closer to the covered market but between the two?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It exploded right outside the entrance to the Markale market, and a year earlier, a shell landed on Markale I. That is the market that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Carter, you stood up in a very agitated mood.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I didn't anticipate being agitated. I just wanted to point out for the Court, at page 26, line 8, Judge Picard's question was not recorded, so we're not certain for the clarity of record what the question was that the witness responded to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge Picard, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could the French booth help us or ... if they can remember what the Judge said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could ask whether the two markets were active during the war?

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thanks, Madam Carter. Any questions arising from Judges' questions, Madam Carter?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That brings us to the end of your testimony, sir. Thank you so much for coming to testify. You are now excused. You may stand down, and please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into -- we are in open session. All we need to do is to pull up the curtain. Madam Carter, next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Cannata will take the next witness, but he's not with us. He's probably en route or -- we anticipated that this examination would continue through 3.30 at least, so we didn't have Mr. Cannata sitting in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have any suggestions what we can do?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What I suggest, we break -- take a break now and then come back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Come back for Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- and Mr. Cannata will be ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. --- Break taken at 3.19 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon once again. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Cannata will call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm here. The next witness is a protected witness. Shall we go -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session. Could we bring down the curtain, please, or the blind, as it is called.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MESUD JUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I would like to put a couple of questions to the witness which have to do with his professional background, could we move into private session for the next couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my colleague Ms. McKenna will call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam McKenna.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: As you move to your podium, Madam McKenna, what is the name of your next witness, or is he a protected witness too?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: The next witness is Mr. Azem Agovic. He is a 92 ter witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And he's not protected?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And he's not protected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May you please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. You may be seated, sir. Your witness, Madam McKenna.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Sir, could you please state your name and date of birth for the record.

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Azem Agovic. I was born on the 12th of July, 1948.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Do you recall testifying in the case against Dragomir Milosevic on 13th February, 2007?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: If we could please have 65 ter 09425 on the screen, and page 3 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Prior to coming here today, was this testimony read back to you in your own language?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Were the contents of the testimony true and correct?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions today, would you answer in the same way?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I please tender this as a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P535.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could please have 65 ter 09423.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Agovic, do you recall giving a statement to the representatives from the Office of the Prosecutor on 21st of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And if we could just scroll down on the English version of this document, so the document on the left-hand side. Do you recognise your signature on that document?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Was this document -- was your statement read back to you in your own language prior to signing it?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity to review the statement prior to your testifying today?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Are the contents of the statement true and correct?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And, once again, if you were asked the same questions today, would you answer them in the same way?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this please be tendered as a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P536.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: If I could please have 65 ter 09424 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Agovic, do you recall giving a further statement to representatives from the Office of the Prosecutor on the 21st of April, 2006?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And do you recognise your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Was the document read back to you in your own language prior to your signing it?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity to review the statement prior to your testifying today?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Once again, if you were answered [sic] the same questions, would you answer them in the same way?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could tender this as a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P537.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Together with your previous testimony before the Tribunal, do these two statements constitute an accurate record of what happened to you on the 3rd of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, I'd like at this stage to read a short summary of the witness's prior testimony into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: The witness's evidence relates to scheduled incident B11 of the indictment. On 3rd March, 1995, the Bajram Muslim holiday, the witness was travelling on a crowded tram between the new part of the city in Novi Grad and the old city in Bascarsija. It was a sunny and clear day. The witness was sitting facing the rear of the tram with the Grbavica neighbourhood to his left. In the vicinity of the Holiday Inn hotel, where the tram lines turn to the outside of the road from the centre, the witness was shot. One bullet entered his body just above the left hip and exited at his right hip. The witness testified that the shooting came from the Grbavica area. A young man and a child were also wounded in the incident. There were no military institutions, military vehicles, or any other military equipment present in the vicinity of the area in which the tram was shot at, neither had there been any military activity in the area that day. The witness was taken to Kosevo Hospital where he was operated on and stayed for 16 days in intensive care. After the incident, the witness's health deteriorated. Initially, he could not walk far, drive a car, or carry heavy things, and he continued to receive treatment for about another three years. Your Honours, if I may, I'd like to ask one or two brief clarificationary questions regarding the testimony that the witness has given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement of 21st November, 1995, you described how you were taken to Kosevo Hospital, where you spent time in intensive care.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: If I could ask that we see 65 ter 04525, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Agovic, this is a letter of admission to the emergency ward of the Kosevo Hospital dated 3rd March, 1995. Can you confirm that this was the date on which you were admitted to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P538.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: If we could please see 65 ter 00181.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Agovic, this is a medical record from the Sarajevo University Clinical Centre regarding the treatment you received for the injury caused by the sniper shot. Could you please explain what type of surgery you underwent?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam McKenna, will the witness be able to answer that question, or should we, rather, refer to this document to see what surgery he underwent?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness does have a recollection of the general type of surgery, but by all means, we can refer to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine. As you please. If you think he can give us an explanation, let him go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, to the best of your ability, can you recall the treatment you received in Kosevo Hospital further to your sniper injury?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, all I can say, that the surgery was very complex because you can see my entire abdomen on the front was open. The scars are still visible where the bullet entered and exited. The surgery took about seven to eight hours, between 11.00 p.m. up until 7.00 a.m., 8.00 a.m., and being an architect I really could not help you with the medical terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: That's understood.

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: No one really believed that I would survive.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: If I may tender this document as an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 65 ter 00181 is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P539.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, this concludes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam McKenna. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Agovic, good afternoon. My name is Novak Lukic, and on behalf of the Defence team for Mr. Perisic, I will be putting several short questions to you. I would just kindly ask you to make a brief pause before answering my question, and I will do the same before I put the next question to you in order to make sure that the interpretation of what we say is accurate. We've already heard two witnesses in relation to this incident in this courtroom before, and we do have a fair idea of what happened. But, nevertheless, you will be given a sketch, and I will ask you to draw the position where you recall the tram was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, unfortunately, all the photographs are already marked in e-court, and this is one copy of a photograph I received courtesy of the OTP, and could we place this on the ELMO for the witness to make a marking on it if he can find his bearings on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. But your --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is 65 ter 8598. Unfortunately, all the copies that were available are already marked in e-court. This is a blank copy, and I can pass it up to my colleagues to inspect it. I just wanted it to be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. Pass it onto your colleagues. While you're doing so -- there we go. We seem to be getting it on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was going ask why can't we get it because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was looking at other photographs, and they were all marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with the location?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see and can you mark the place where you believe the tram was shot at and when you were wounded on this photograph? The usher will hand you a special pen, and you will place a small cross on the screen itself, marking the location where you believe the tram was. You were moving from the right side to the left, from downtown to the suburbs?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: From Ilidza towards Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: And this is where the tram crosses from the middle of the street where the track ran to the right-hand side of the street, and this is where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please place a cross on the spot?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher please erase the obviously erroneous blue line in the continuation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Agovic, you felt a blow. Did you hear a shot being fired before that, or did you not hear anything? Do you recall this? It's been a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: When the first shot was fired, I only felt the pain, but I did not hear that first shot which hit me. I only heard the shots that ensued.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please be asked to approach the microphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That same bullet?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: No. The person next to me was hit by another bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And how do you know that it was a different bullet that hit the person next to you?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Because the bullet that hit me remained in my body, so it must have been another bullet that hit the other person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because only one hole, a bullet-hole, was found on the tram during the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm an architect. I'm not familiar with these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement, which is now Exhibit P5536, this is the first statement you gave in 1995, and you say - that's the last paragraph of the statement: "The bullet that hit me was fired from a building in Zagrebacka Street on the very edge where Grbavica starts." If we blow up the photograph, can you locate --

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: The building was called Matalka. I didn't go over there to take look at it, but that's what the story was, that there was a sniper up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was something you heard from the various stories?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have any desire to go and see for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At any rate, you had the information on the basis of what you heard, that there were snipers in that building?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: When I recovered and I began walking again, that was when I heard the story, not before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you've -- you didn't finish your answer. You learned about it when you got out of the hospital, but before that?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never did go over there. I would not have been on a tram had there not been a truce in force at the time because the trams otherwise would not have run through the area. There was a truce on, and that's why the trams were running along the tracks, and after that incident, they did not run before the Dayton Accords were passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That's all. Thank you, Witness. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Any re-examination, Madam McKenna?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I would just like to make a clarification or a correction, rather, to the transcript at page 58, line 2. The direction should read Bascarsija to Ilidza. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you confirm that with the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Witness, could you please confirm which direction the tram was travelling when you were shot.

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: From Ilidza to Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were facing in the direction of?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: It was facing Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And which area was to your left?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Grbavica was to my left.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And from which direction were -- were you hit?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: From the left side.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just one question, sir, or one little issue. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did I hear you correct that you had an entry wound and an exit wound on the other side of -- on the other hip, on the right hip?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In answer to a question by counsel for the Defence, you said that the bullet that hit you remained in your body, so it must have been another bullet that hit the other person. My question is: If it remained in your body, how do you get an exit wound?

utterances.speaker: AZEM AGOVIC
utterances.text: The physicians took it out. It was stuck in the tissue. As it went and hit the right hip bone, it remained stuck there, hanging in the skin tissue or the trousers or whatever. I'm not sure about this fully, where exactly it was, because it was the doctor who took it out and showed it to me, and you can see the exit wound. You can see both the entry and the exit wounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We accept what you say. We will not want to look at your hip at this stage. Thank you so much. Any questions arising from the Bench's questions? Madam McKenna? Thank you. Sir, that brings us to the end of your testimony for today. You are now excused, and you may stand down. Please travel well back home. That concludes your evidence, and thank you so much for coming to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. That is all the witnesses the Prosecution has available today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For the day?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we then stand adjourned to Monday the 9th at 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom I. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 9th day of February, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.12 p.m.,
